questions.question: Does a model give the same answer every time it gets the same prompt?

options.text: Yes, with the same prompt it always says the same thing
Not necessarily: sampling makes answers vary from run to run

questions.why: Sampling makes answers vary, so one good run proves little about the next one.

questions.question: What does a model remember between two calls?

options.text: Only what the harness sends in this call

questions.why: A model is stateless. Each call carries the whole prompt, so the harness keeps the history and resends it.

questions.question: What is a context window?

options.text: The number of messages in a chat
The most tokens the model can read in one call
A browser tab that holds the chat

questions.why: Everything in one call, the prompt and the tools included, has to fit inside the window.

questions.question: What makes a chatbot into an agent?

options.text: It asks for tools, the harness runs them, and it calls the model again

questions.why: The model asks; the harness acts; the loop goes on until something stops it.

questions.question: When should an agent loop stop?

options.text: Only when the model says it is done
When the model is done, or a limit stops it first

questions.why: A model saying it is done is a claim. The harness needs limits too: a turn limit and a budget.

questions.question: Who decides whether a requested tool actually runs?

options.text: The harness, under its permission rules

questions.why: The model asks for a tool. The harness checks its rules, then runs the tool or refuses it.
